landing.heroDescription: The Right to Information Act gives every Indian citizen the right to ask the government for information. We make it simple.
landing.step1Desc: Tell us what happened in plain language. No legal knowledge needed.
landing.step2Desc: Our tool turns your complaint into a specific, legally sound RTI request.
landing.step3Desc: We route your request to the correct government office — Central or State.
landing.step4Desc: The government must respond within 30 days. We help you track it.
landing.painPoint1Desc: We route it correctly — Central or State.
landing.painPoint2Desc: We score it and draft your first appeal.
landing.painPoint3Desc: Describe your problem — we write the request.
landing.faq1A: The Right to Information Act 2005 gives every Indian citizen the legal right to request information from any government body. The government must respond within 30 days.
landing.faq2A: ₹10 for most states. Some states charge ₹50. BPL (Below Poverty Line) cardholders file for free.
landing.faq3Q: What if the government doesn't reply?
landing.faq3A: If there's no reply within 30 days, you can file a First Appeal. If that fails, you can escalate to the Information Commission.
landing.faq4A: RTI applications must include your name and address, but the purpose need not be disclosed. Your identity is protected by law.

about.introDesc: Under the RTI Act, every Indian citizen has the right to ask any government body for information. The government must respond within 30 days.
about.whatCanAskDesc: Any information held by a public authority — documents, files, emails, meeting minutes, spending records, decisions.
about.rightsSummaryDesc: You can ask any government body for any document, and they must give it to you — or give you a lawful reason why not.
about.update1Desc: The central portal has integrated a new seamless appeal process for requests that have crossed the 30-day limit without a response.
about.update2Desc: Citizens with verified BPL (Below Poverty Line) status can now bypass the fee payment gateway automatically via their synced documents.
about.update3Desc: You can now draft your RTI in English and translate it automatically to regional languages like Hindi, Bengali, or Tamil directly in the final step.
about.clearRulesDesc: When filing an RTI, keep your questions specific and related to existing records.
about.rule1Ex: Example: "Provide a copy of the road repair budget" (Good) vs "Why is the road so bad?" (Bad)
about.rule2Desc: Be specific with dates and details.
about.rule2Ex: Example: "Ration card applications received in Jan 2024" (Good) vs "All ration card applications" (Bad)
about.rule3Ex: Keep it straightforward. You don't need complex legal jargon.
about.cannotFileTitle: When an RTI CANNOT be filed
about.cannotFileDesc: The RTI Act exempts certain types of information from being disclosed.
about.cannot1Desc: You cannot file an RTI against private bodies like private schools, hospitals, or corporate companies (unless they are substantially funded by the government).
about.cannot2Desc: Information that would affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India.
about.cannot3Desc: Details of other citizens that have no relationship to any public activity or interest (invasion of privacy).
about.cannot4Desc: You cannot ask questions like "When will the road be built?". You can only ask for records of decisions already made.
about.heroSubtitle: Empowering citizens to seek answers, simply and effectively.

ai.subtitle: Your RTI Legal Assistant · Voice + Chat
ai.faq2: How do First and Second Appeals work?
ai.faq3: Is RTI free for BPL citizens?
ai.faq5: What if no reply in 30 days?
ai.ans1: Under the RTI Act 2005, the Public Information Officer (PIO) must respond within **30 days** of receiving your application. For matters involving life or liberty, the deadline is **48 hours**.
ai.ans2: If the PIO does not reply in 30 days or gives incomplete info, you can file a First Appeal. If unsatisfied with the First Appeal, you can escalate via a Second Appeal to the Information Commission.
ai.ans3: Yes! Citizens holding a valid **BPL (Below Poverty Line) card** are completely exempt from the ₹10 application fee and all document copying charges. Your DigiLocker vault auto-verifies this.
ai.ans4: Absolutely. You can file Central Government RTIs at **rtionline.gov.in**. Many state portals also support online filing. Our app guides you through the exact process step by step.
ai.ans5: Silence is deemed a **refusal** under the RTI Act. You can immediately file a First Appeal citing non-response, and even escalate to the Central Information Commission (CIC) for a Second Appeal.
ai.ans6: Our AI routing engine analyzes your problem and identifies the exact **Ministry and Public Information Officer (PIO)**. Just describe your issue and hit 'File RTI' — we'll figure out the right desk.
ai.defaultAns: I'm cross-referencing the RTI Act and public archives... Based on established guidelines, you have strong grounds here. Want me to draft the exact application for you?
